- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > -0.28 over recent days), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; reduce forecast peak by 10–15% to account for mean reversion.
- If sentiment is positive but recent prices are trending down, model may lag in recognizing reversal; add 1–2 days of downward bias to forecast to align with sentiment shift.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overestimates volatility; cap forecast range within ±1.5–2.0 standard deviations of recent 7-day mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period price increases (especially after sentiment turns positive); add 0.5–1.0 point bias toward higher end in final 5–7 days.
- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.17 for 3+ consecutive days), model often fails to capture momentum; increase forecast slope or add 1–2% upward bias in final 7–10 days.
